sources.title: MAX31865 RTD-to-Digital Converter data sheet
sources.locator: page 10, Detailed Description / Application Circuits / Using Thermistors
supports: signal conditioning optimized for PT100 through PT1000 RTDs
ADC output equals RTD resistance divided by reference resistance
four-times-R0 reference resistor guidance for platinum RTDs
PT100 uses 400 ohm and PT1000 uses 4 kohm as nominal optimum examples
other resistive sensors may be used when RREF is at least the sensor maximum resistance
4-wire connection eliminates cable-resistance error by separate force and sense leads

manufacturer_support.rationale: Analog Devices explicitly documents platinum RTDs from PT100 through PT1000 and 4-wire sensor connections; the assessed 430 ohm reference resistor is within the documented operating range.

electrical_compatibility.rationale: The assessed RREF is within the documented operating range, the complete required resistance envelope remains below RREF and the 15-bit full-scale ratio, the upper envelope threshold remains representable without downward rounding, and the resulting 4-wire bias-current bounds remain inside the documented output-current range.

project_validation.rationale: No qualifying physical MAX31865 plus RTD-family validation record is yet referenced for this configuration.

limitations: This record assesses a 4-wire topology only; 2-wire and 3-wire accuracy and lead-resistance effects are not classified by this record.
Electrical compatibility establishes acquisition-range feasibility, not RTD probe product ratings, temperature accuracy, or physical project validation.
